migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC migration program governance, assign a technical lead, and document the DoD mandate requirements (NIST-standardized ML-KEM and ML-DSA only) and the 2027 deadline.
Perform cryptographic inventory of the IKEv2/IPsec VPN estate: identify all gateways, endpoints, firmware versions, RSA-2048 and DH Group 14 usage, certificate authorities, and PSK usage.
prerequisites: Network management access to VPN devices

migration_steps.activity: Evaluate the vendor's PSK appliance claim: confirm it does not support ML-KEM or ML-DSA, document that PSK with 256-bit entropy is not a NIST-standardized PQC algorithm, and record the gap against the DoD mandate.

Issue formal RFI to current VPN vendor and alternative vendors requesting evidence of ML-KEM and ML-DSA support in IKEv2/IPsec, including IETF RFC status, firmware versions, and certification evidence.
Assess network team PQC skills gap and deliver foundational PQC training covering ML-KEM, ML-DSA, hybrid key exchange, and IKEv2/IPsec integration.

Define target VPN architecture: hybrid key establishment using ML-KEM combined with classical DH, and ML-DSA for authentication/signatures where supported, aligned to NIST standards and DoD acceptance criteria.
Select vendor(s) with confirmed ML-KEM and ML-DSA support in IKEv2/IPsec; require written evidence of standards compliance and interoperability test results.
Procure PQC-capable VPN hardware/software and required licenses; schedule delivery outside the Dec 1–Jan 15 change freeze.
Build non-production lab environment and validate ML-KEM hybrid key exchange and ML-DSA authentication interoperability with DoD endpoints and contractor infrastructure.
Conduct security assessment and DoD acceptance testing of the PQC VPN configuration; obtain written DoD approval for the algorithm suite.
Develop production cutover plan, rollback plan, and maintenance windows that respect the Dec 1–Jan 15 change freeze; schedule production changes for after 2026-01-15.
Execute production migration of VPN gateways to ML-KEM hybrid key exchange and ML-DSA authentication in phased maintenance windows after the change freeze.
Perform post-migration verification, monitoring, and documentation update; confirm all VPN traffic uses DoD-accepted NIST PQC algorithms ahead of the 2027 deadline.

blockers.blocker: Vendor appliance does not support ML-KEM or ML-DSA.
blockers.reason: DoD mandate explicitly requires NIST-standardized PQC algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA); PSK is not a NIST-standardized PQC algorithm and does not satisfy the mandate.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain vendor roadmap with committed dates for ML-KEM and ML-DSA support, or select an alternative vendor with confirmed support and evidence.

blockers.blocker: DoD acceptance of PQC algorithm suite not yet obtained.
blockers.reason: Production deployment cannot proceed without written DoD approval of the specific ML-KEM/ML-DSA configuration.
blockers.resolution_required: Complete DoD acceptance testing and obtain written approval before production cutover.

blockers.blocker: Network team has no PQC experience.
blockers.reason: Misconfiguration of hybrid key exchange or signature algorithms risks interoperability failure and security gaps.
blockers.resolution_required: Complete PQC training and lab validation before production changes.

blockers.blocker: Change freeze from Dec 1 to Jan 15.
blockers.reason: Production changes cannot occur during the freeze, constraining the migration window.
blockers.resolution_required: Schedule all production changes after 2026-01-15 and complete non-production work before 2025-12-01.

blockers.blocker: Interoperability with DoD endpoints using ML-KEM/ML-DSA not yet validated.
blockers.reason: DoD may use specific hybrid or pure PQC profiles that must match contractor configuration.
blockers.resolution_required: Conduct joint interoperability testing with DoD and document supported algorithm identifiers and profiles.

vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Formal statement of non-support and any future roadmap; not acceptable for DoD mandate compliance as-is.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: To be determined via RFI; must provide evidence of NIST-standardized ML-KEM and ML-DSA support.

algorithm_roles.ML-KEM: Post-quantum key establishment (key encapsulation) for IKEv2/IPsec, used in hybrid mode with classical DH to establish session keys resistant to Shor's algorithm.
algorithm_roles.ML-DSA: Post-quantum digital signatures for authentication of IKEv2 peers and integrity protection, replacing or augmenting RSA signatures where supported.
